issues.legal_issue: A licensee whose licence derived from a tenant does not obtain statutory tenant status when the tenant’s interest and the licence have ended before the qualifying date.
material_facts: The petitioners claimed statutory protection as licensees under an agreement with the tenant.
The tenant’s contractual tenancy ended after notice, and her statutory tenancy ended when the ejectment decree was passed, both before the qualifying date.
The petitioners’ licence depended on the tenant’s interest in the premises and had ended with that interest.
issues.conclusion: The petitioners were not licensees under a subsisting agreement on the qualifying date and were not entitled to become tenants of the landlord under the statutory protection claimed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 5(4A), 14(2) and 15A(1) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, a licensee must be in occupation under a subsisting licence on the qualifying date to claim the statutory benefit. A licence granted by a tenant ordinarily ends when the tenant’s interest ends; section 14(2) operates from the loss of the licensee’s status and may then make the erstwhile licensee a tenant of the landlord on the terms of the licence. Madhusudan A. Mahale v. P.M. Gidh was held inapplicable.

rule.if: licensee_protection_claim and licence_granted_by_tenant and licensor_tenancy_ended_before_qualifying_date and licence_ended_with_licensor_tenancy

predicates.licensee_protection_claim: The occupant claimed statutory protection on the basis of being a licensee.
predicates.licence_granted_by_tenant: The occupant’s licence was granted by a person who held the premises as a tenant.
predicates.licensor_tenancy_ended_before_qualifying: The licensor’s tenancy ended before the date on which the occupant had to qualify for statutory protection.
predicates.licence_ended_with_licensor_tenancy: The occupant’s licence ended when the licensor’s tenancy and interest in the premises ended.

issues.definition: When an occupant claims protection as a licensee under a tenant, but the tenant’s tenancy and the derived licence ended before the qualifying date, the occupant is not entitled to statutory tenancy.

issues.legal_issue: A subtenant obtains statutory tenant protection only if the premises were lawfully sublet before the applicable statutory cutoff.
material_facts: The petitioner claimed that he had occupied the entire flat as a subtenant from an earlier time and had merely confined his occupation to the portion in question later.
The courts below found that his occupation of the portion then in his possession began in 1962, not earlier.
The subtenancy of that portion therefore began after the applicable cutoff.
issues.conclusion: The petitioner was not entitled to statutory protection as a subtenant and had no right to continue in possession on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, protects a subtenant to whom the premises were lawfully sublet before commencement of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 1959. Because the courts found that the subtenancy of the premises in question began after that cutoff, the petitioner could not claim the benefit of section 14(1).

predicates.subtenant_protection_claim: The occupant claimed statutory protection on the basis of being a subtenant.
predicates.subtenancy_began_after_statutory_cutoff: The subtenancy of the premises in the occupant’s possession began after the applicable statutory cutoff.

issues.definition: If an occupant claims statutory protection as a subtenant and the subtenancy began after the applicable cutoff, the occupant is not entitled to statutory tenancy or continued possession on that basis.
